text: A person who receives God's will and passes it on to others. Samuel, Gad, and Nathan did this work at David's side.
Pouring olive oil on someone's head, a sign that God had appointed that person as king or priest.
A person who offered sacrifices in the sanctuary and stood before God on behalf of the people. The office belonged to Aaron's descendants.
Worshiping God by offering animals or grain, to seek forgiveness for sin or to give thanks.
A sacrifice burned whole on the altar to God, expressing complete devotion.
An offering celebrating peace between God and people. Part of the meat was shared and eaten together.
A raised platform where offerings were burned for God, built of earth or stone.
An animal, grain, or other gift presented to God in a sacrifice.
An ancient stringed instrument with strings stretched on a wooden frame and plucked by hand. David played it well.
An ancient plucked stringed instrument, used with the lyre in worship and at celebrations.
A small hand drum. Women often played it as they danced and sang.
An instrument made of two bronze plates struck together, like modern cymbals.
The length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, about 45 cm. Six cubits and a span is close to 3 meters.
A unit of weight and of money; one shekel is about 11 g. Armor of five thousand shekels weighs over 50 kg.
The largest unit of weight: one talent is about 34 kg, equal to 3,000 shekels.
Circumcision was a rite of cutting off a baby boy's foreskin, a sign of belonging to the people in covenant with God.
The skin covering the tip of the penis. The Philistines were not circumcised, so foreskins proved that they had been killed.
A small, human-shaped figure of a god kept in the home. In Israel it was a forbidden idol.
An image made by human hands and worshiped as a god. The Bible says to worship no god but God.
A vest-like garment worn by priests. It was used to ask God's will, and David sought guidance through it.
The holy place where God was worshiped and sacrifices were offered. In David's day it was at Nob.
Bread set out before God on the table in the sanctuary. It was replaced every Sabbath, and only priests ate it.
The portable tent sanctuary used for worship since the wilderness years, until the temple was built.
A dwelling made of cloth. David pitched a separate tent to house the ark.
Large cloths that formed a tent or screened off a space. Here it means the ark was kept inside a tent.
A gold-covered chest holding the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments. It showed that God was among his people, and it was not to be touched carelessly.
The house for worshiping God. David prepared for the temple in Jerusalem, and his son Solomon built it.
A solemn promise both sides bind themselves to keep. God made an everlasting covenant with David's family.
A name of God meaning the Lord who commands all the armies of heaven and earth.
'The Lord' stands for Yahweh, the personal name God revealed to Moses, usually understood as 'the one who is'.
The Spirit of God. When he came upon a person, he gave strength and wisdom to do God's work.
Being seized by God's Spirit to speak his word or to sing his praise; not only predicting the future.
The first day of a new lunar month. Israel offered sacrifices and held a feast on that day.
A weapon with a leather pouch: a stone is put in it, swung around, and let fly. Shepherds also used it to drive off wild animals.
A short spear made for throwing.
An officer in command of a thousand soldiers.
The highest officer, leading the nation's whole army.
Horse-drawn war carts. They also displayed the power and status of a king or prince.
A wide, flat area where harvested grain was beaten to loosen the kernels, usually on a windy hilltop.
Fine white cloth woven from thin thread, used for priests' garments.
A large, fragrant, hard-wooded tree from Lebanon, prized timber for building palaces and the temple.
Wealth that a defeated nation paid every year to the nation that conquered it.
An adviser who gave the king plans and opinions. Ahithophel was famous for his wisdom.
A promise a person freely makes to God to do something. It had to be kept.
Taking a dispute to court to get a judgment.
A small tree that grows well even in dry land.
Going without food for a time, out of grief or in earnest prayer.
Bowing down before God to honor and adore him.
The commandments and rules God gave through Moses, showing Israel the way to live.
A large, broad rock; a picture of God, who protects and never moves.
One of the twelve clans of Israel descended from the twelve sons of Jacob.
Older leaders who guided towns and tribes.
The whole people gathered together for worship or for an important event.
Members of the tribe of Levi, who carried and cared for the tabernacle and the ark.
God's holy anger, which does not let sin go unpunished.
A bag made of sewn animal hide, used to carry wine or water.
Wheat or barley kernels roasted to make food that was easy to carry and eat.
Food made by thickening animal milk, similar to yogurt or butter.
A gift the groom gave to the bride's family. Saul used it as an excuse to put David in danger.
A person who kept watch from a wall or a high place and announced anyone approaching.
A person who ran to deliver news or orders in haste.
Upholding what is right and fair in God's eyes. A good king had to rule with justice.
Setting something aside from ordinary use to give it to God alone.
Behavior and bearing fitting one's position and rank.
A large tree of the oak family that bears acorns, with wide, tangled branches.
An animal born of a horse and a donkey. In David's time kings and princes rode them.
The book of the Bible that gathers songs and prayers offered to God. Many of them were written by David.
Love and favor freely given to someone who has not earned it.
